key_concept: Electron-withdrawing groups such as $-NO_2$ at the para position increase the acidity of benzoic acid, while electron-donating groups such as $-CH_3$ at the para position increase the basicity of aniline.
steps: Statement I, the reaction: acidic $KMnO_4$ oxidises the side-chain $-CH_3$ to $-COOH$. The ring and the $-NO_2$ group are untouched, so p-nitrotoluene gives p-nitrobenzoic acid ($O_2N-C_6H_4-COOH$).

Statement I, the acidity: the para $-NO_2$ group withdraws electrons by both $-I$ and $-R$ effects. This stabilises the carboxylate anion, making p-nitrobenzoic acid ($pK_a \approx 3.4$) stronger than benzoic acid ($pK_a \approx 4.2$). Statement I is correct.
Statement II, the reaction: $Sn/HCl$ reduces $-NO_2$ to $-NH_3^+Cl^-$. Neutralisation with base then frees the amine, giving p-toluidine ($CH_3-C_6H_4-NH_2$).

Statement II, the basicity: the para $-CH_3$ group donates electrons by $+I$ and hyperconjugation. This raises the electron density on the nitrogen lone pair, so p-toluidine ($pK_b \approx 8.9$) is more basic than aniline ($pK_b \approx 9.4$). Statement II is correct.
Both statements are correct, so the answer is Option (1), which matches the official key.
final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
why_not_others: Options (2), (3) and (4) each mark at least one statement as wrong. In fact, the para-$NO_2$ group really does raise acidity and the para-$CH_3$ group really does raise basicity relative to the unsubstituted parent compounds.
common_trap: Students compare p-nitrobenzoic acid's basicity instead of its acidity, or wrongly assume that $Sn/HCl$ or $KMnO_4$ alters both substituents rather than only the intended group.
time_saving_tip: Write each product directly: $KMnO_4$ oxidises only the $-CH_3$ group, and $Sn/HCl$ reduces only the $-NO_2$ group. Then apply the rule: an EWG makes an acid stronger, and an EDG makes an amine more basic.
